vulnerability.name: GHSA-qwgh-2vcv-g2f7
vulnerability.description: block-buffer: a panic caught inside a compression or block-generation callback leaves the cursor stored in the buffer's block out of bounds

statements.impact_statement: block-buffer 0.10.4 is in Cargo.lock and crates/agentd/fuzz/Cargo.lock only through digest 0.10.7, under blake2 0.10.6 and sha2 0.10.9 (snow) and sha1 0.10.7 (aws-config, axum, tungstenite); `cargo tree -i block-buffer@0.10.4 --target all` lists them. The 0.12.1 copy in Cargo.lock is the fixed release. The advisory's corruption needs the cursor to live inside the data block: 0.12.0's EagerBuffer keeps it in the block's last byte and its ReadBuffer in byte 0, so input copied in before a panicking callback overwrites it. 0.10.4 keeps the cursor in its own `pos: u8` field (src/lib.rs:61-62), which only `set_pos_unchecked` writes, after each callback returns (`digest_blocks`, `set_data`, `digest_pad`), and it has no ReadBuffer, so a caught panic leaves the previous, valid position. The advisory's EagerBuffer proof of concept, built in debug mode against both releases on 2026-10-27, read cursor 2 after the caught panic on 0.10.4 and failed the cursor invariant on 0.12.0. Re-check if either lockfile gains block-buffer 0.11.x or 0.12.0, if a 0.10.x release moves the cursor into the block, or if the advisory names a 0.10 code path.
statements.status_notes: Since 2026-10-30 GitHub and osv.dev list GHSA-qwgh-2vcv-g2f7's affected range as >= 0.11.0, < 0.12.1, so no scanner matches block-buffer 0.10.4 and the root and crates/agentd/fuzz osv-scanner.toml files no longer ignore it. The statement stays as the record of the 2026-10-27 analysis, which still holds for 0.10.4.

vulnerability.name: GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249
vulnerability.description: minimatch: at optimizationLevel 2 or above, a pattern's `**/../` segments multiply its glob parts during preprocessing, and the pairwise pass over them then takes quadratic time

statements.impact_statement: minimatch 10.2.6 is in site/pnpm-lock.yaml only, required as ^10.2.5 by typedoc 0.28.20 (also reached through typedoc-plugin-markdown 4.13.1), the docs site's devDependency that renders the TypeScript SDK reference from site/scripts/reference/sdk/typescript.mjs; `pnpm why minimatch` in site/ lists that one path, and nothing in site/ ships in a crate, wheel or npm package. The advisory's growth happens in firstPhasePreProcess and secondPhasePreProcess, which minimatch calls only when a caller sets optimizationLevel to 2 or more (dist/esm/index.js:332-341; the default is 1). typedoc builds every Minimatch with `{ dot: true }` or no options (dist/node-utils.js:62, :83 and :318), and `grep -rl optimizationLevel` over the dist directories of typedoc 0.28.20 and typedoc-plugin-markdown 4.13.1 finds no file, so that branch never runs. No semver-compatible fix exists: the fix is minimatch 11.0.1, which removes matchOne(), and typedoc's glob() calls it (dist/node-utils.js:328). Re-check when typedoc or typedoc-plugin-markdown is bumped or another package in the site lockfile starts to depend on minimatch, and drop this statement once typedoc requires minimatch 11.
